answer: Each new identity must lock a uniqueness bond that unlocks only after the same key posts daily signed heartbeats for 21 days, each heartbeat hashing the previous one so the chain cannot be forked later. Like a lotus that opens only after long still growth, clones lose because the ledger keeps solely the first valid tip. Auditors inspect a karst of heartbeat chambers; a missing day or reused hash collapses the bond. An opal of copied keys fails that hash-link check, so extra identities cost waiting time rather than extra keys.
